name: Regular Black Hole from Pure Gravity
short_name: Regular Black Hole from Pure Gravity

coordinates.name: Hyperspherical, Five Dimensions

parameters.description: Mass as Tangherlini's radius, $r_0^2 = m = 8GM/(3\pi c^2)$, with $G$ Newton's constant in five dimensions
Length of the de Sitter core, $\ell^2 = \alpha$ the coupling of the quasi-topological tower, with $f \approx 1 - r^2/\ell^2$ near the centre

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, r, \psi, \theta, \phi)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time, and take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$. A dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$. For $r_0 > 2\ell$ the horizons $r_- < r_+$ are the two positive roots of $r^4 - r_0^2r^2 + \ell^2r_0^2$, $r_\pm^2 = \tfrac{1}{2}\left(r_0^2 \pm r_0\sqrt{r_0^2 - 4\ell^2}\right)$.

coordinates.name: Ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein, Five Dimensions

parameters.description: Mass as Tangherlini's radius, $r_0^2 = m = 8GM/(3\pi c^2)$, with $G$ Newton's constant in five dimensions
Length of the de Sitter core, $\ell^2 = \alpha$ the coupling of the quasi-topological tower, with $f \approx 1 - r^2/\ell^2$ near the centre

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(v, r, \psi, \theta, \phi)$, with the advanced time $v = ct + r_*$ a length, where $dr_*/dr = \left(1 - r_0^2r^2/(r^4 + \ell^2r_0^2)\right)^{-1}$ and $r_* = 0$ at $r = 0$. For $r_0 > 2\ell$ the horizons $r_- < r_+$ are the two positive roots of $r^4 - r_0^2r^2 + \ell^2r_0^2$, $r_\pm^2 = \tfrac{1}{2}\left(r_0^2 \pm r_0\sqrt{r_0^2 - 4\ell^2}\right)$.
